## Setting up accounts and tools

In this path you send the metadata XML files to the
[SD Submit API](https://github.com/CSCfi/metadata-submitter) yourself, using the command
line tools `curl` and `jq`. You also need an account for the BigPicture login portal.

| Tool | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| [`curl`](https://curl.se) | Send requests to the SD Submit API |
| [`jq`](https://jqlang.org) | Read the JSON responses, and pick out the submission ID when creating the submission |


## Login portal account

You get the access token for the API from the
[BigPicture login portal](https://login.bp.nbis.se/), which you log in to with
your [LS AAI](../../../services/lsaai.qmd) account. Logging in requires
multi-factor authentication (MFA). If your home organization doesn't already
provide MFA,
[set it up in LS AAI](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1l_RLIeVmZZNccU0fwDuSSHaSMVlnMA4XddyZULw7zN4/edit#heading=h.b3p1rl8mrgjf).
Uploading to production also requires a signed Terms of Use.

## Authenticate to the SD Submit API

Go to the [BigPicture login portal](https://login.bp.nbis.se) and complete OIDC authentication.

Then copy the access token shown _"For **uploading** to the Inbox"_ and use it for all
subsequent API calls in the authorization header. The same token is needed when publishing,
since the API then uploads the metadata files to your Inbox on your behalf.

```bash
# Set the JWT as env variable (access token copied above)
export TOKEN="..."

# Set the API URL as env variable
export API_URL="https://metadata-submitter.bp.nbis.se"

# To test a submission in the staging environment, use the url below:
# export API_URL="https://metadata.staging.bp.nbis.se"

# If you have deployed the API locally for testing, uncomment the line below and set this as:
# export API_URL="http://localhost:5431"

# Ensure the API recognizes the user based on the access token with:
curl --request GET "$API_URL/v1/users" \
     --header "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" | jq
```
